sections.title: 2.1 Product Perspective
sections.text_preview: The EVLA Correlator Backend System will be designed and implemented as a real-time data processing system. The system is expected to be implemented on a distributed memory cluster of connected process

sections.title: 2.2.3 Data Output

sections.title: 2.2.4 Monitoring
sections.text_preview: The Correlator Backend System will conduct a number of self-monitoring activities on application and system software as well as hardware systems to detect system failure and out of spec conditions.

sections.title: 2.2.5 Recovery
sections.text_preview: The ability to attempt recovery from failure and out of spec performance conditions will be built into the system.

2.3 User characteristics
sections.text_preview:
All use of the Correlator Backend System will be indirect via the Monitor and Control System.   
The BE system will not directly produce any user interface screens.

sections.title: 2.3.1 Array Operator
sections.text_preview: The primary contact with array operations will be via status and error messages channeled through the Monitor and Control System.

sections.title: 2.3.2 Engineers and Technicians

sections.title: 2.3.4 Software Developer
sections.text_preview: These individuals are responsible for developing the software and will interact with the system to ensure that it is functioning properly. The software developer requires remote access to the system s

sections.title: 2.3.5 Web User
sections.text_preview: A few authorized individuals may be allowed access to parts of the system that are usually considered restricted

sections.title: 2.4.1 Criticality of the Application
sections.text_preview: The Correlator Backend System is a critical component in the Astronomical data path. If it is unavailable, incoming astronomical data will be lost.

sections.title: 2.4.4 Communications Limitations
sections.text_preview: The ability to realize and maintain real-time operations is critically dependent upon the performance levels of available network systems.

sections.title: 2.4.5 Processing Limitations
sections.text_preview: Operations performed shall be reversible. That is, the original raw uncorrected data must be recoverable from the processing output.
